what: Zscaler sells cloud security. Instead of routing a company's traffic through hardware in its own offices, traffic goes through Zscaler's global network, which inspects it and decides what is allowed. This is the model known as zero trust.
customers: Large enterprises and government agencies securing employees working anywhere.
money: cloud security subscriptions priced per user
moat: A global network of data centres inspecting traffic at scale, which took years to build, plus the fact that replacing it means re-architecting how a company connects its people to its applications.
risks: It still makes an operating loss because of very large stock-based compensation
Palo Alto and Microsoft bundle competing capabilities into broader platforms
Growth has slowed from its earlier pace
Analyst targets imply the shares are roughly fairly valued
opportunities: Revenue grew about 25% last year and about 28% a year over three years
Gross margin of 77% with strong free cash flow despite the accounting loss
Securing artificial intelligence applications and agents is a new product area
watch: Billings growth and the number of customers spending over $1 million a year.
